name: Where Civilization Began
description: The first farmers, cities, scripts and kingdoms in the river valleys of the Near East, South Asia and China, and the great collapse that ended the Bronze Age.

checkpoints.name: Before the cities
checkpoints.note: Hunters built the temple at Gobekli Tepe, and people settled at Jericho and Catalhoyuk. The Neolithic brought farming, and irrigation let villages grow in dry lands.

checkpoints.name: Sumer and the first inventions
checkpoints.note: In Sumer the first cities rose. People used the plough and the wheel, wrote on clay in cuneiform, and learned to smelt bronze, while Egyptians began to write hieroglyphs.

checkpoints.name: Kings, laws and epics
checkpoints.note: The Indus cities like Mohenjo-daro had a script of their own. Sargon of Akkad built an empire, the Epic of Gilgamesh was composed, Hammurabi of Babylon issued his code, and scribes counted in base 60, a system inherited from Sumer.

checkpoints.name: The Bronze Age ends
checkpoints.note: The Hittites, a giant eruption on Thera and the first Chinese characters belong to an age of great powers. Around 1200 BCE many of them fell in the Late Bronze Age collapse.

checkpoints.name: The first empires
checkpoints.note: Phoenician sailors spread an alphabet. Assyria kept a library at Nineveh, Nebuchadnezzar rebuilt Babylon and its gardens, and Cyrus the Great founded the Achaemenid Empire.
